The major in Arabic introduces students to each of these varieties of Arabic and to their respective literatures.</p><p><br></p><p>Listed below are the lower division major preparation courses for the major.</p><p><br></p><p>To be considered for admission to this major, you must complete the following courses by the end of spring before transfer:</p><ul><li>One year of college level coursework in the declared language OR</li><li>At least one year of high school in which the primary language of instruction was the declared language.</li></ul><p>Completion of two years of college level foreign language is <strong>STRONGLY RECOMMENDED</strong>.</p><p>A placement exam is required for all language majors regardless of credits earned in lower division language courses.</p><p>All courses must be taken for a letter grade.</p><p><br></p><p>For information regarding preparation for this major, visit <u style=\"color: rgb(41, 98, 255);\">https://</u><a href=\"http://nelc.ucla.edu/arabic\" rel=\"noopener noreferrer\" target=\"_blank\">nelc.ucla.edu/arabic</a> and <u style=\"color: rgb(41, 98, 255);\">https://</u><a href=\"http://www.admission.ucla.edu\" rel=\"noopener noreferrer\" target=\"_blank\">admission.ucla.edu</a>.</p><p><br></p><p>PLEASE NOTE: the community college courses listed below have been approved to satisfy the preparation for this major at UCLA, but they may not be exact equivalents of the UCLA courses.</p>","groupId":"68c26f45-6887-ef11-8474-000d3a37e3b6","position":1,"area":"General"}]},{"name":"Architectural Studies/B.A.","templateAssets":[{"type":"GeneralTitle","content":"IMPORTANT MAJOR INFORMATION","groupId":"46c26f45-6887-ef11-8474-000d3a37e3b6","position":0,"area":"General"},{"type":"GeneralText","content":"<p>The focus of the Architectural Studies major is on the built environment. The curriculum conceives of architecture as a cultural, creative, and technical practice and a discipline with direct social impact. Within the context of a liberal arts education, a finely balanced set of architecture and urban design courses ranging from the history and theory of design to contemporary building technologies will provide students with a diverse foundation of knowledge in the field of architecture and prepare them for graduate school and /or careers in a wide range of fields.</p><p><br></p><p>Admission to Architectural Studies is highly selective: we receive many applications for limited spots. The most important admission criteria are the supplemental application which involves additional essays, a portfolio, strong academic performance, and evidence of community engagement relative to interest in the major.</p><p><br></p><p>The availability of arts coursework at community colleges can differ, so you may not find exact equivalents for all classes. However, this will not negatively affect your admission. Look for the closest matches in your curriculum, and if a course wasn't completed at your current institution, you can take it at UCLA. Substitutions for lower-division requirements will be determined by the department in the summer following admission. Syllabi or other descriptive course documentation may be required for consideration. </p><p><br></p><p>Recommended (not required) preparation for the major*:</p><ul><li>Two courses in the history of architecture {Pre-history-Mannerism and 1600-present} and</li><li>One Introduction to Architecture course.</li></ul><p>*It is common for transfers to complete these courses at UCLA. </p><p><br></p><p>Supplemental Requirements:</p><p>In addition to the general UC Application, applicants must submit a supplement that consists of additional essays and a portfolio. Additional fees may apply.</p><p><br></p><p>All students must have a cumulative 3.0 GPA at the time of application.</p><p><strong>Students MUST complete the requisite two English courses and one Math course by the end of Spring prior to transfer.</strong> Students are encouraged to take their required English and Math courses as early as possible with at least one English course completed by the end of Fall.</p><p><br></p><p>Completion of IGETC is not required, but strongly recommended. to professional art training within the context of a research university. The department provides students with a broad experience to the arts and encourages new fields of investigation. Students work in more than one medium and explore mixed media possibilities as well in areas of painting, drawing, sculpture, ceramics, new genres, and theory. The program's intent is to provide the framework, both through coursework and independent study, to assist each student in developing their own body of work.</p><p><br></p><p>Admission to Art is highly selective: we receive many applications for limited spots. The most important admission criteria are the <strong>supplemental application</strong> which involves additional essays, a portfolio, and evidence of community engagement relative to interest in the major.  </p><p><br></p><p>The availability of arts coursework at community colleges can differ, so you may not find exact equivalents for all classes. However, this will not negatively affect your admission. Look for the closest matches in your curriculum, and if a course wasn't completed at your current institution, you can take it at UCLA. Substitutions for lower-division requirements will be determined by the department in the summer following admission. Syllabi or other descriptive course documentation may be required for consideration.</p><p><br></p><p><br></p><p>Recommended (not required) preparation for the major*:</p><ul><li>One course each in Drawing, Sculpture, Painting, Photography, Ceramics, and New Genres (performance art, video art, installation, and non-studio work).</li><li>Four courses (total) in Art History, including one course covering each of the following art historical periods, preferably with a global context: 1850-1920s, 1920s-1960s, 1960s-present.</li></ul><p>*It is common for transfers to complete these courses at UCLA. </p><p><br></p><p>Supplemental Requirements:</p><p>In addition to the general UC Application, applicants must submit a supplemental application that consists of additional essays and a visual arts portfolio. many facets of life.</p><p><br></p><p>Listed below are the lower division preparation information courses for the major.</p><p><br></p><p>To be considered for this major, you must complete the The biomedical engineering, biomolecular engineering, environmental engineering, and semiconductor manufacturing engineering options provide students with an opportunity for exposure to a subfield of chemical and biomolecular engineering. In all cases, balance is sought between engineering science and practice.</p><p><br></p><p>Admission to the Henry Samueli School of Engineering and Applied Science (HSSEAS) at UCLA is highly competitive. The most important selection criteria are completion of the required preparatory courses and academic performance. All applicants must have a minimum transferable cumulative GPA of 3.4. HSSEAS admits students by major and does NOT consider applicants for alternate majors.</p><p><br></p><p>To be considered for admission to this major, you must complete the following courses by the end of spring before transfer:</p><ul><li>One and a half years of Calculus through Multivariable,</li><li>One course in Linear Algebra,</li><li>One course in Differential Equations,</li><li>One year of General Chemistry with Labs,</li><li>One year of Organic Chemistry,</li><li>One and a half years of Calculus Based Physics series [for Engineering majors] with Lab, and</li><li>One course in Java, C, C++ or MATLAB.</li></ul><p>All courses must be taken for a letter grade.</p><p><br></p><p>Applicants are not required to complete the HSSEAS General Education Requirements in order to be admitted, although it is beneficial for students to complete 1 course from each of the following areas: arts, humanities, social sciences, and life sciences. Applicants can fulfill the lower division General Education requirements by completion of the Intersegmental General Education Transfer Curriculum (IGETC). Partial IGETC is NOT accepted.</p><p><br></p><p>For more information regarding this major and UCLA transfer selection process, visit <u style=\"color: rgb(41, 98, 255);\">https://</u><a href=\"http://www.admission.ucla.edu%20or/?\" rel=\"noopener noreferrer\" target=\"_blank\">admission.ucla.edu.</a> If you still have specific questions, you may email the HSSEAS admissions office at <a href=\"mailto:ugradadm@seas.ucla.edu\" rel=\"noopener noreferrer\" target=\"_blank\">ugradadm@seas.ucla.edu</a>.</p><p><br></p><p>PLEASE NOTE: The community college courses listed on this major agreement have been approved as substitutes to satisfy the admission preparation requirements for this major, but they may not be exact equivalents of the UCLA courses listed. people within the U.S., as well as of other Latina/Latino and indigenous populations in the Americas. Addressing local, national, and transnational contexts, the Chicana/Chicano and Central American Studies curriculum at UCLA explores race, class, gender, and sexuality paradigms as they have shaped the history of the field, as well as new directions in the study of Chicanas/Chicanos and Latinas/Latinos, including (1) border and transnational studies, (2) expressive arts, (3) history, literature, and language of Americas, and (4) labor, law, and policy studies.</span></p><p><br></p><p>Listed below are the lower division preparation courses for the major.</p><p><br></p><p>To be considered for This program is an excellent foundation for entry into professional practice in civil engineering or for more advanced study.</p><p><br></p><p>Admission to the Henry Samueli School of Engineering and Applied Science at UCLA (HSSEAS) is highly competitive. The most important selection criteria are completion of the required preparatory courses and academic performance. All applicants must have a minimum transferable cumulative GPA of 3.4. HSSEAS admits students by major and does NOT consider applicants for an alternate major.</p><p><br></p><p>To be considered for this major, you must complete the following courses by the end of spring before transfer:</p><ul><li>One and a half years of Calculus through Multivariable,</li><li>One course in Linear Algebra,</li><li>One course in Differential Equations,</li><li>One year of General Chemistry with Lab,</li><li>One and a half years of Calculus Based Physics series [for Engineering majors] with Lab, and</li><li>One course in Java, C, C++ or MATLAB.</li></ul><p>All courses must be taken for a letter grade.</p><p><br></p><p>Applicants are not required to complete the HSSEAS General Education Requirements in order to be admitted, although it is beneficial for students to complete 1 course from each of the following areas: arts, humanities, social sciences, and life sciences. Applicants can fulfill the lower division General Education requirement by completion of the Intersegmental General Education Transfer Curriculum (IGETC). Partial IGETC is NOT accepted.</p><p><br></p><p>For more information regarding this major and UCLA's transfer selection process, visit <u style=\"color: rgb(41, 98, 255);\">https://</u><a href=\"http://www.admission.ucla.edu/\" rel=\"noopener noreferrer\" target=\"_blank\">admission.ucla.edu</a>. While including a strong foundation in the traditional areas of psychology, the major is interdisciplinary in nature and emphasizes subject matter within cognitive psychology, computer science, mathematics, and related disciplines. </span></p><p><br></p><p>Listed below are the lower division preparation courses for the major. Students are classified as Pre-Cognitive Science until all preparation courses are completed at UCLA. Transfer students must be directly admitted as Pre-Cognitive Science in order to major in Cognitive Science. Note: You must be directly admitted in to this major and cannot change into this major after admission to UCLA.</p><p><br></p><p>To be considered for this major, you should complete the following seven courses by the spring before transfer:</p><ul><li>One year of Calculus,</li><li>One course in Introduction to C++, and</li><li>Four courses from the following:</li><li class=\"ql-indent-1\">Introductory Psychology</li><li class=\"ql-indent-1\">Introductory Biology or Biology for the major</li><li class=\"ql-indent-1\">One course from Introductory Physics, Chemistry or Linguistics</li><li class=\"ql-indent-1\">Philosophy (Critical Reason, Science of the Mind or Logic)</li><li class=\"ql-indent-1\">Additional Intermediate Level Computing courses</li></ul><p>All courses must be taken for a letter grade.</p><p>Applicants for Fall 2024 and beyond must complete seven courses, including one computing course, by end of spring before transfer.</p><p><br></p><p>For more information regarding this major and UCLA's selection process, visit <u style=\"color: rgb(41, 98, 255);\">https://www.psych.ucla.edu</u> and <u style=\"color: rgb(41, 98, 255);\">https://</u><a political contexts.</p><p><br></p><p>Listed below are the lower division preparation courses for the major.</p><p><br></p><p>To be considered for this major, you must complete the following courses by the end if spring before transfer:</p><ul><li>One course in English Composition (Expository Writing);</li><li>One course in Critical Reading and Writing (Composition and Literature),</li><li>Two survey courses in World or English literature (at least one must be world literature), and</li><li>Two years of one Foreign Language.</li></ul><p>All courses must be taken for a letter grade.</p><p><br></p><p>For more information regarding this major and UCLA's transfer selection process, visit <u style=\"color: rgb(41, 98, 255);\">https://</u><a href=\"http://www.complit.ucla.edu\" computer science, a minor or technical support area, and a core of courses from the social sciences, life sciences, and humanities. Students study subject matter in software engineering, principles of programming languages, data structures, computer architecture, theory of computation and formal languages, operating systems, distributed systems, computer modeling, computer networks, compiler construction, and artificial intelligence.</p><p><br></p><p>Admission to the Henry Samueli School of Engineering and Applied Sciences at UCLA is highly competitive. The most important selection criteria are completion of the required preparatory courses and academic performance. Listed below are the lower division preparation courses for the major. All applicants must have a minimum transferable cumulative GPA of 3.4. Preparatory courses must be completed by the end of spring prior to fall enrollment. HSSEAS admits students by major and does NOT consider applicants for alternate majors.</p><p><br></p><p>To be considered for this major, you must complete the following courses by the end of spring before transfer:</p><ul><li>One and a half years of Calculus through Multivariable,</li><li>One course in Linear Algebra,</li><li>One course in Differential Equations,</li><li>One and a half years of Calculus Based Physics series [for Engineering majors] with Lab, and</li><li>One course in C++ (strongly preferred), C or JAVA.</li></ul><p>All major courses must be taken for a letter grade.</p><p><br></p><p>Applicants are not required to complete the HSSEAS General Education Requirements in order to be admitted, although it is beneficial for students to complete 1 course from each of the following areas: arts, humanities, social sciences, and life sciences. Applicants can fulfill the lower division General Education requirement by completion of the Intersegmental General Education Transfer Curriculum (IGETC). Partial IGETC is NOT accepted.</p><p><br></p><p>For more information regarding this major and UCLA's transfer selection process, visit <u style=\"color: rgb(41, 98, 255);\">https://</u><a href=\"http://www.admission.ucla.edu/\" rel=\"noopener noreferrer\" target=\"_blank\">admission.ucla.edu</a>. Department of World Arts and Cultures/Dance is at the forefront of innovative, interdisciplinary, and cross-cultural studies of the arts, offering a curriculum in which students can explore the vital relationship of the arts and performance to cultural theory and criticism. The Dance major thoroughly integrates learning to dance, learning to make dances, and critical interrogation of dance as a cultural practice. Students study a variety of techniques from around the world throughout their studies. They enroll in a four-term sequence in dance composition, with additional opportunities to participate in the creation of their own dances, as well as working as dancers in the creation of new works by faculty members and visiting artists. Furthermore, they engage in a core of four courses in the study of scholarly discourse around the body and dance, launching a critical inquiry into their own study of bodily practices, internalization of the embodied experience, and how bodily ideas and embodied experiences are interpreted and communicated outwardly and interpersonally, both locally and globally.</p><p><br></p><p>Admission to Dance is selective: we receive many applications for limited spots. The most important admission criteria are the supplemental application which involves a dance audition, additional essays, strong academic performance, and evidence of community engagement relative to interest in the major.</p><p><br></p><p>The availability of arts coursework at community colleges can differ, so you may not find exact equivalents for all classes. However, this will not negatively affect your admission. Look for the closest matches in your curriculum, and if a course wasn't completed at your current institution, you can take it at UCLA. Substitutions for lower-division requirements will be determined by the department in the summer following admission. Syllabi or other descriptive course documentation may be required for consideration.</p><p><br></p><p>Recommended (not required) preparation for the major*:</p><ul><li>One course each in improvisation/choreography, dance history and theory</li><li>At least eight courses [approximately 12 semester/ 20 quarter units] in various dance techniques particularly modern/postmodern dance, Hip-Hop, West African, Ballet, or coursework focusing on using dance as a medium to connect and engage the community.</li></ul><p>*Most transfer students complete these courses at UCLA. </p><p><br></p><p>Supplemental requirements:</p><p>In addition to the general UC Application, applicants must submit a supplement which consists of an audition, additional essays, and other creative materials. Additional fees may apply. We will also be looking for strong academic preparation and evidence of involvement in the arts and community that demonstrates interest in varied cultures. </p><p><br></p><p>All students must have a cumulative 3.0 GPA at the time of application.<strong> </strong></p><p><strong>Students MUST complete the requisite two English courses and one Math course by the end of Spring prior to transfer.</strong> Students are encouraged to take their required English and Math courses as early as possible with at least one English course completed by the end of Fall. analytical theoretical, and technology-mediated work in design and media arts. Please note that this is NOT a graphic design major, but an academic program that supports a diversity of interests around design, media, technology, and culture. Our integrative curriculum invites students to balance their aesthetic sensibility with logical reasoning, formal theories with practical application, and contemporary thought with a historical perspective. Most transfer students take three years to complete the program.</p><p><br></p><p>Admission to Design | Media Arts is highly selective: we receive many applications for limited spots. The most important admission criteria are the supplemental application which involves additional essays, a design portfolio, strong academic performance, and evidence of community engagement relative to interest in the major. </p><p><br></p><p>Please refer to the FAQs for transfer students that DMA has prepared, which outlines learning outcomes for their lower division classes and possible equivalents from community college: <a href=\"https://www.uclaarts-admission.com/design-media-arts#dma_transfers\" rel=\"noopener noreferrer\" target=\"_blank\">https://www.uclaarts-admission.com/design-media-arts#dma_transfers</a>. Look broadly across your available course curriculum, in any and all areas having to do with art, architecture, design, computer science, information systems, multimedia, interactivity, communications, journalism, et al, to identify possible matches for coursework in drawing, color theory, two-dimensional and three-dimensional form, digital media/computer design, programming for media arts, letterforms and typography, design history, design culture, and interactivity and media arts.</p><p><br></p><p>The availability of arts coursework at community colleges can differ, so you may not find exact equivalents for all classes. However, this will not negatively affect your admission. Look for the closest matches in your curriculum, and if a course wasn't completed at your current institution, you can take it at UCLA. Substitutions for lower-division requirements will be determined by the department in the summer following admission. Syllabi or other descriptive course documentation may be required for consideration. </p><p><br></p><p>Recommended (not required) preparation for the major*:</p><ul><li>One course each in drawing, color theory, two-dimensional and three-dimensional form, digital media/computer design, programming for media arts, letter forms and typography, design history, design culture, and interactivity and media arts.</li></ul><p>*Most transfer students complete these courses at UCLA.</p><p><br></p><p>Supplemental Requirements:</p><p>In addition to the general UC Application, applicants must submit a supplement that consists of a visual arts portfolio and additional writing statements. Additional fees may apply.  </p><p><br></p><p>All students must have a cumulative 3.0 GPA at the time of application.</p><p><strong>Students MUST complete the requisite two English courses and one Math course by the end of Spring prior to transfer.</strong> Students are encouraged to take their required English and Math courses as early as possible with at least one English course completed by the end of Fall. Completion of IGETC is not required but strongly recommended.</p><p><br></p><p>More information may be found at <u style=\"color: rgb(41, 98, 255);\">https://</u><a href=\"http://www.arts.ucla.edu/apply\" rel=\"noopener noreferrer\" target=\"_blank\">arts.ucla.edu/apply</a>. is more important than ever and UCLA’s School of Education and Information Studies is at the forefront of that conversation. As the top-ranked public program in education in the nation, the Department of Education is guided by a commitment to integrate theory and practice and to improve educational practice and policy. The department attracts prominent scholars and is internationally recognized for its research centers in evaluation, higher education, child development, and urban education. Whether students choose to pursue a PHD, an EDD, Masters or Bachelors degree, or a teaching or administrative credential, they graduate with a broad understanding of educational theory and tested practice.</p><p><br></p><p>The Department is known as a leader in the study and practice of urban education, student testing and assessment, teacher and continuing education and development (particularly in urban, multi-ethnic environments), early childhood development, and issues of access, equity, and quality facing K-12 and higher education. Here, faculty and students work together to solve the most pressing issues facing education today. signals and systems, circuits and embedded systems, and physical wave electronics. These collectively provide an understanding of inventions of importance to society, such as integrated circuits, embedded systems, photonic devices, automatic computation and control, and telecommunication devices and systems. </span></p><p><br></p><p><span style=\"font-size: 12px;\">Admission to the Henry Samueli School of Engineering and Applied Science (HSSEAS) at UCLA is highly competitive. The most important selection criteria are completion of the required preparatory courses and academic performance. Listed below are the lower division preparation courses for the major. All applicants must have a minimum transferable cumulative GPA of 3.4. Preparatory courses must be completed by the end of spring prior to fall enrollment.</span></p><p><br></p><p><span style=\"font-size: 12px;\">To be considered for this major, you must complete the following courses by the end of spring before transfer:</span></p><ul><li>One and a half years of Calculus through Multivariable,</li><li>One course in Linear Algebra,</li><li>One course in Differential Equations,</li><li>One course in General Chemistry with Lab,</li><li>One and a half years of Calculus Based Physics series [for Engineering majors] with Lab, and</li><li>One course in C++, C or JAVA.</li></ul><p>All courses must be taken for a letter grade.</p><p><br></p><p>HSSEAS admits students by major and does NOT consider applicants for alternate majors. Applicants are not required to complete the HSSEAS General Education Requirements in order to be admitted, although it is beneficial for students to complete 1 course from each of the following areas: arts, humanities, social sciences, and life sciences. Applicants can fulfill the lower division General Education requirements by completion of the Intersegmental General Education Transfer Curriculum (IGETC). Partial IGETC is NOT accepted.</p><p><br></p><p>For more information about this major and UCLA's transfer selection process visit, <u style=\"color: rgb(41, 98, 255);\">https://</u><a href=\"http://www.admission.ucla.edu/\" rel=\"noopener noreferrer\" target=\"_blank\">admission.ucla.edu</a>. Ethnomusicology B.A. major combines hands-on musical experience with academic study to explore the rich variety of musical expressions throughout the world, including Africa, Europe, the Americans, West, East, South, and Southeast Asia with concentrations. The UCLA Herb Alpert School of Music aspires to educate the whole student through productive collaborations between performance and scholarship, a cross-cultural, global understanding of music, and preparatory training. Transfer applicants to the school are considered on the basis of academic achievement as well as departmental screening requirements and must have a minimum 3.2 GPA at the time of application.</p><p><br></p><p>California community college students are strongly encouraged, but not required, to complete IGETC; all other transfer students are encouraged to make progress toward completion of the school’s general education requirements.</p><p><br></p><p>Recommended preparation for the major:</p><ul><li>A one year comprehensive music theory course sequence, covering musicianship (ear training and sight singing), as well as keyboard skills, <strong>OR </strong>One year of music theory and One year of musicianship (ear training and sight singing)</li><li>Two years of participation in a large performance group such as an orchestra, choir, or wind ensemble</li></ul><p>Exemptions/substitutions for lower division requirements will be determined by the department in the summer following admission. Syllabi or other descriptive course documentation may be required for consideration.</p><p><br></p><p>Audition/interview and Supplemental Requirements: In addition to the UC Application, applicants are required to submit supplemental application materials which vary by major and are used in a prescreening process to determine which students will be invited to interview and/or audition. and South America, and elsewhere, allows for a more pointed, rigorous, and comprehensive understand of history and more accurate contextualization of the \"European\" experience in the world.</p><p><br></p><p>Listed below are the lower division preparation courses for the major.</p><p><br></p><p>To be considered for this major, you must complete the following courses by the end of four-year Bachelor of Arts degree in Film and Television provides an education in the history and theory of these art forms and basic learning experiences in production within the context of a liberal arts education.</p><p><br></p><p>In the first year, students are introduced to all major aspects of film, television, and digital media study. In the second year, each student completes a senior concentration chosen from film production, television production [narrative or documentary], screenwriting, animation, cinema and media studies or digital media. Students must also complete at least one professional internship. Undergraduates in the film and television program take courses in: cinema and media studies- the history, theory, and aesthetics of both film and television; production- film, television (studio and field), digital, experimental, and animation; and film and television craft- writing, directing, cinematography and editing.</p><p><br></p><p>Recommended courses prior to entrance include:</p><ul><li>American Film History,</li><li>European Film History,</li><li>American Television History, and</li><li>One Theater course.</li></ul><p>Additional admission requirements include a personal essay, a critical essay, a creative writing sample a life challenge essay and two letters of recommendation. Film, videotapes, DVD's and links are not accepted.</p><p><br></p><p>Prior experience is not required. Applicants to the school must have a minimum 3.2 GPA at the time of application and must complete their general education coursework prior to entrance. The classes include principles of geophysics, earthquake physics, seismology, fault mechanics, and seismic exploration with state-of-art quantitative tools.</span></p><p><br></p><p>Listed below are the lower division preparation courses for the major.</p><p><br></p><p>To be considered for this major, you must complete the following courses by the end of spring term before transfer:</p><ul><li>One introductory course in Earth Sciences with Lab,</li><li>One General Physics course with Lab for Majors, and</li><li>One year of Calculus.</li></ul><p>Completion of a  third semester of calculus and a second semester of calculus-based physics with lab is <strong>STRONGLY RECOMMENDED</strong>.</p><p>All courses must be taken for a letter grade.</p><p><br></p><p>For more information regarding this major and UCLA's transfer selection process, visit <a href=\"http://www.ess.ucla.edu\" rel=\"noopener noreferrer\" target=\"_blank\">https://epss.ucla.edu</a> and <u style=\"color: rgb(41, 98, 255);\">https://</u><a href=\"http://www.admission.ucla.edu\" rel=\"noopener noreferrer\" target=\"_blank\">admission.ucla.edu</a>.</p><p><br></p><p>PLEASE NOTE: the community college courses listed below have been approved to satisfy the preparation for this major at UCLA, but they may not be exact equivalents of the UCLA courses listed.</p>","groupId":"42b06f45-6887-ef11-8474-000d3a37e3b6","position":1,"area":"General"}]},{"name":"Global Jazz Studies/B.A.","templateAssets":[{"type":"GeneralTitle","content":"IMPORTANT MAJOR INFORMATION","groupId":"6dc26f45-6887-ef11-8474-000d3a37e3b6","position":0,"area":"General"},{"type":"GeneralText","content":"<p>The Global Jazz Studies major encourages students to think globally about the capacity of jazz to transform the musical and political worlds it engages, while building upon UCLA’s strong jazz studies and world music foundation. The UCLA Herb Alpert School of Music aspires to educate the whole student through productive collaborations between performance and scholarship, a cross-cultural, global understanding of music, and preparatory training for a broad range of careers in music following graduation. Transfer applicants to the school are considered on the basis of academic achievement as well as departmental screening requirements and must have a minimum 3.2 GPA at the time of application.</p><p><br></p><p>California community college students are strongly encouraged, but not required, to complete IGETC; all other transfer students are encouraged to make progress toward completion of the school’s general education requirements. In addition to the UC Application, applicants are required to submit supplemental application materials which vary by major and are used in a prescreening process to determine which students will be invited to interview and/or audition.</p><p><br></p><p>Recommended (not required) preparation for the major:</p><ul><li>A one-year comprehensive Music Theory course sequence, incorporating Musicianship (ear training and sight singing), as well as Keyboard Skills, or</li><li>One year of Music Theory, and</li><li>One year of Musicianship (ear training and sight singing).</li><li>A one to two years of Applied Jazz Studio instruction (private lessons).</li></ul><p>In addition to the UC Application, applicants are required to submit supplemental application materials which vary by major and are used in a prescreening process to determine which students will be invited to interview and/or audition.</p><p><br></p><p>The UCLA Herb Alpert School of Music houses the supplemental application on the Acceptd platform - <u style=\"color: rgb(41, 98, 255);\">https://app.getacceptd.com/herbalpert</u>. style=\"font-size: 14px;\">Courses in the Global Studies major study processes and consequences of increasing inter-connectivity in matters related to the expansion of the world economy, the demands for new forms of international cooperation and governance among states, and the mixing of cultures associated with the increased mobility of populations and the wide dissemination of information and media images.</span></p><p><br></p><p>Transfer students are admitted as Pre-Global Studies majors and must submit a supplemental application to the Global Studies Major during their first term at UCLA. A minimum of one year of foreign language proficiency should be completed prior to matriculation. Two years are required to graduate.</p><p><br></p><p>To be considered for this major, you must complete the following courses by the end of the spring before transfer:</p><ul><li>Complete a <strong><u>MINIMUM OF SIX</u></strong><u> </u>preparatory courses by the end of spring before transfer:</li><li class=\"ql-indent-1\">One course in Introduction to Globalization,</li><li class=\"ql-indent-1\">One Statistics course,</li><li class=\"ql-indent-1\">At least One Year of College-level Foreign Language, and</li><li class=\"ql-indent-1\">Five courses with no more than two from any of the following three categories: Culture and Society, Governance and Conflict, or Markets and Resources.</li></ul><p>By the end of the Fall Term of admission, students must complete Global Studies 1 and all remaining preparatory courses with a B grade or better and submit a supplemental application.</p><p>All courses must be taken for a letter grade.</p><p><br></p><p>For more an interdisciplinary approach to learning about current issues at the intersections of human biology, genomics and society. THIS IS A HIGHLY SELECTIVE MAJOR.</p><p><br></p><p>To be considered for this major, you must complete the following courses by the end of the spring before transfer:</p><ul><li>One year of Biology for major with Laboratory,</li><li>One year of General Chemistry with Laboratory,</li><li>One year of Calculus, and</li><li>One semester of Organic Chemistry with Lab.</li></ul><p>Completion of a second semester of organic chemistry or one year of calculus based physics is <strong>STRONGLY RECOMMENDED</strong>. Labor Studies major offers UCLA undergraduates an opportunity to learn about the workplace and the social, political, and economic forces that influence it. The program places emphasis on the labor market, public policy, employment relations, unions, and working-class movements. It also explores issues of race, class, and gender in the workplace. By critically analyzing the theory and practice of current workplace issues, students develop a deeper understanding of the relationships between their education and society at large and how they, as college graduates, can transform the nature of work. </p><p><br></p><p>Listed below are the lower division preparation courses for the major.</p><p><br></p><p>To be considered for this major, you must Marine Biology major is the study of marine organisms and their environment. Students in the Marine Biology major are required to participate in the Marine Biology Quarter (MBQ). The MBQ provides the opportunity for undergraduates to live the life of a marine biologist. Under the guidance of department faculty and graduate assistants, the students design their own research projects, reside and collect data at a field station, conduct experiments to test their hypotheses, and present their work at the end of the quarter.</p><p><br></p><p>Listed below are the lower division major preparation courses for the major as well as important details to review. THIS MAJOR IS HIGHLY SELECTIVE.</p><p><br></p><p>To be considered for this major, you must complete the following courses by the end of spring before transfer:</p><ul><li>One year of Biology with Laboratory,</li><li>One year of General Chemistry with laboratory,</li><li>One year of Calculus, and</li><li>One semester of Organic Chemistry with Laboratory.</li></ul><p>Completion of a second semester of Organic Chemistry or one year of Calculus Based Physics is <strong>STRONGLY RECOMMENDED</strong>. If your college does not offer a two semester or three quarter sequence in Calculus Based Physics, it is recommended that you complete Physics 5ABC at UCLA after you transfer.</p><p>All courses must be taken for a letter grade.</p><p><br></p><p>For more information regarding this major and UCLA's transfer selection process, visit <u style=\"color: rgb(41, 98, 255);\">https://</u><a href=\"http://www.eeb.ucla.edu/undergraduate.php\" rel=\"noopener noreferrer\" target=\"_blank\">eeb.ucla.edu/undergraduate.php</a> and <u style=\"color: rgb(41, 98, 255);\">https://</u><a href=\"http://www.admission.ucla.edu\" rel=\"noopener noreferrer\" target=\"_blank\">admission.ucla.edu</a>.</p><p><br></p><p>PLEASE NOTE: the community college courses listed below have been approved to satisfy the preparation requirements for this major at UCLA, but they may not be exact equivalents of the UCLA courses listed.</p>","groupId":"28b66f45-6887-ef11-8474-000d3a37e3b6","position":1,"area":"General"},{"type":"GeneralText","content":"<p>UCLA's life science majors require the completion of extensive preparatory coursework prior to transfer, therefore, you must be admitted directly into a life science major; you will not be able to change from a non-life science major into a life science major after admission to UCLA.</p><p><br></p><p>Students who have placed out of UCLA's Math 31A course based on AP/IB credit may be required to complete UCLA's Math 3C, 32A or an equivalent course after transfer.</p><p><br></p><p>The community college statistics course included on this agreement has been approved as a substitute for Statistics 13, however it may not transfer as an exact UCLA equivalent.</p><p><br></p><p>UCLA's Chem 153A is an upper-division course that satisfies a major requirement but is NOT required for admission. pursue a professional career in the materials field and desire a broad understanding of the relationship between microstructure and properties of materials.</p><p><br></p><p>Admission to the Henry Samueli School of Engineering and Applied Science (HSSEAS) at UCLA is highly competitive. The most important selection criteria is completion of the required preparatory courses and academic performance. Listed below are the lower division preparation courses for the major. All applicants must have a minimum transferable, cumulative GPA of 3.4. Preparatory courses must be completed by the end of the spring term prior to fall enrollment.</p><p><br></p><p>To be considered for this major, you must complete the following courses by the end of spring before transfer:</p><ul><li>One and a half years of Calculus through Multivariable,</li><li>One course in Linear Algebra,</li><li>One course in Differential Equations,</li><li>One year of General Chemistry with Lab,</li><li>One and a half years of Calculus Based Physics series [for Engineering majors] with Lab, and</li><li>One course in Java, C, C++ or MATLAB.</li></ul><p>All major prep courses must be taken for a letter grade.</p><p><br></p><p>HSSEAS admits students by major and does NOT consider applicants for alternate majors. Applicants are not required to complete the HSSEAS General Education Requirements in order to be admitted, although it is beneficial for students to complete 1 course from each of the following areas: arts, humanities, social sciences, and life sciences. Applicants can fulfill the lower division General Education requirement by completion of the Intersegmental General Education Transfer Curriculum (IGETC). Partial IGETC is NOT accepted.</p><p><br></p><p>For more information regarding this major and UCLA's transfer selection process, visit <a href=\"http://www.engineer.ucla.edu./\" rel=\"noopener noreferrer\" target=\"_blank\">https://samueli.ucla.edu</a> and <u style=\"color: rgb(41, 98, 255);\">https://admission.ucla.edu</u>. The most important selection criteria are completion of the required preparatory courses and academic performance. Listed below are the lower division preparation courses for the major. All applicants must have a minimum transferable, cumulative GPA of 3.4. Preparatory courses should be completed by the end of spring prior to the fall enrollment.</p><p><br></p><p>To be considered for this major, you must complete the following courses by the end of spring before transfer:</p><ul><li>One and a half years of Calculus through Multivariable,</li><li>One course in Linear Algebra,</li><li>One year of General Chemistry with Lab,</li><li>One and a half years of Calculus Based Physics series [for Engineering majors] with Lab, and</li><li>One course in Java, C, C++ or MATLAB.</li></ul><p>All major prep courses must be taken for a letter grade.</p><p><br></p><p>HSSEAS admits students by major and does NOT consider applicants for alternate majors. Applicants are not required to complete the HSSEAS General Education Requirements in order to be admitted, although it is beneficial for students to complete 1 course from each of the following areas: arts, humanities, social sciences, and life sciences. Applicants can fulfill the lower division General Education requirement by completion of the Intersegmental General Education Transfer Curriculum (IGETC). The microorganisms that form the core of this curriculum, bacteria, eukaryotic parasites, and viruses, are agents of disease, but they also are critical to our health, food system, biotechnology (e.g. biofuels), and the environment. Our immune system controls health and disease, by detection and destruction of microorganisms and cancer cells, and is also a core of the curriculum. </span>To this, our research and curriculum seeks a detailed molecular genetic understanding of both microorganisms and the immune system to address the most pressing questions in the field. </p><p> In addition to key core courses, the MIMG major emphasizes learning through an authentic research experience. All our students carry out primary research, either by working in a faculty member’s laboratory, or through collaborative research projects in laboratory courses. Through this research experience, we will help you develop skills needed in your future careers, including the ability to present your research in both written and oral forms. </p><p><br></p><p>Listed below are the lower division preparation courses for the major as well as important details to review. THIS MAJOR IS HIGHLY SELECTIVE.</p><p><br></p><p>To be considered for this major, you must complete the following courses by the end of spring before transfer:</p><ul><li>One year of Biology for major with Laboratory,</li><li>One year of General Chemistry with Laboratory,</li><li>One year of Calculus, and</li><li>One semester of Organic Chemistry with Lab.</li></ul><p>Completion of a second semester of Organic Chemistry or one year of Calculus Based Physics is <strong>STRONGLY RECOMMENDED</strong>. (If your college does not offer a two semester or a three quarter sequence in calculus based physics, it is recommended that you complete Physics 5ABC at UCLA after transfer).</p><p>All courses must life science majors require the completion of extensive preparatory coursework prior to transfer, therefore, you must be admitted directly into a life science major; you will not be able to change from a non-life science major into a life science major after admission to UCLA.</p><p><br></p><p>Students who have placed out of UCLA's Math 31A course based on AP/IB credit may be required to complete UCLA's Math 3C, 32A or an equivalent course after transfer.</p><p><br></p><p>The community college statistics course included on this agreement has been approved as a substitute for Statistics 13, however, it may not transfer as an exact UCLA equivalent.</p><p><br></p><p>UCLA's Chem 153A is an upper-division course that satisfies a major requirement but is NOT required for admission. After transferring, <strong><u>students must petition</u></strong> for transfer credit and should contact the academic advisor for their major for additional support and details about this process.</p>","groupId":"61bc6f45-6887-ef11-8474-000d3a37e3b6","position":3,"area":"General"},{"type":"RequirementTitle","content":"LOWER DIVISION MAJOR REQUIREMENTS","groupId":"422c7745-6887-ef11-8474-000d3a37e3b6","position":0,"area":"Requirements"},{"type":"GeneralTitle","content":"ADDITIONAL NOTES","groupId":"6cbc6f45-6887-ef11-8474-000d3a37e3b6","position":2,"area":"General"},{"type":"GeneralText","content":"<p><span style=\";\">The Molecular, Cell, and Developmental Biology major provides undergraduate students with cutting-edge information on the molecular process involved in cell function and differentiation. The curriculum consists of several core and elective disciplines that are updated yearly to reflect advances in the field. </span></p><p><br></p><p>Listed below are the lower division preparation courses for the major as well as important details to review. THIS MAJOR IS HIGHLY SELECTIVE.</p><p><br></p><p>To be considered for this major, you must complete the following courses by the end of spring before transfer:</p><ul><li>One year of Biology for major with Laboratory,</li><li>One year of General Chemistry with Laboratory,</li><li>One year of Calculus, and</li><li>One semester of Organic Chemistry with Lab.</li></ul><p>Completion of a second semester of Organic Chemistry or one year of Calculus Based Physics is <strong>STRONGLY RECOMMENDED</strong>. (If your college does not offer a two semester or three quarter sequence in calculus based physics, it is recommended that you complete Physics 5ABC at UCLA after transfer).</p><p>All courses must be taken for a letter grade.</p><p><br></p><p>For more information about this major and UCLA's transfer selection process, visit <a href=\"http://www.eeb.ucla.edu/undergraduate.php\" rel=\"noopener noreferrer\" target=\"_blank\" style=\"color: rgb(41, 98, 255);\">https://mcdb.ucla.edu</a> and <u style=\"color: rgb(41, 98, 255);\">https://admission.ucla.edu</u>.</p><p><br></p><p>PLEASE NOTE: the community college courses listed below have been approved to satisfy the preparation requirements for this major at UCLA, but they may not be exact equivalents of the UCLA courses listed below.</p>","groupId":"6fbc6f45-6887-ef11-8474-000d3a37e3b6","position":1,"area":"General"},{"type":"GeneralTitle","content":"AP/IB EXAM CREDIT","groupId":"9c218ed7-5f97-47e4-adff-019b946a532c","position":4,"area":"General"},{"type":"GeneralText","content":"<p>The AP Exam Scores listed below may be used to satisfy the major prep:</p><ul><li>A score of <strong><u>5 on the AP Calculus AB exam</u></strong> will satisfy MATH 31A.</li><li>A score of <strong><u>4 on the AP Calculus BC exam</u></strong> will satisfy MATH 31A.</li><li>A score of <strong><u>5 on the AP Calculus BC exam</u></strong> will satisfy MATH 31A and 31B.</li></ul><p><br></p><p>The IB Exam Scores listed below may be used to satisfy the major prep:</p><ul><li>A score of <strong><u>6 or higher on the IB HL Math Analysis & Approaches exam</u></strong> will satisfy MATH 31A.</li></ul>","groupId":"51807d51-a067-4175-81c2-019b946a532c","position":5,"area":"General"}]},{"name":"Music Composition/B.A.","templateAssets":[{"type":"GeneralText","content":"<p>The Music Composition major welcomes composers who demonstrate extraordinary intellectual curiosity and whose primary goal is to communicate with others on a profoundly human level. The program emphasizes the collaborative relationship between composers and performers in such a way that a simulated professional experience is achieved. This major is specifically interested in welcoming composers who demonstrate extraordinary intellectual curiosity and whose primary goal is to communicate with others on a profoundly human level. The program emphasizes the collaborative relationship between composers and performers in such a way that a simulated professional experience is achieved. The school’s renowned composition faculty expect students to acquire and master basic skills, which involves an intensive study of: music theory (written and oral), counterpoint, orchestration, analysis, technology, performance, the traditional Western canon and its history, in tandem with the study of popular, jazz, rock, folk, and nonwestern traditions. Students who successfully complete the B.A. at UCLA are prepared to enter the professional world as practicing artists, film composers, or to continue with graduate studies at the highest level.</p><p><br></p><p>Recommended (not required) preparation for the major:</p><ul><li>A one year comprehensive Music Theory course sequence, covering Musicianship (ear training and sight singing) as well as Keyboard Skills; or</li><li>One year of Music Theory and one year of Musicianship (ear training and sight singing),</li><li>Two years of Applied Studio Instruction on a primary instrument or in voice (private lessons),</li><li>Two years of participation in a large performance group such as Orchestra, Choir, or Wind Ensemble.</li></ul><p><br></p><p>In addition to the UC Application, applicants are required to submit supplemental application materials which vary by major and are used in a pre-screening process to determine which students will be invited to interview and/or audition.</p><p><br></p><p>The UCLA Herb Alpert School of Music houses the supplemental application on the Acceptd platform - <u style=\"color: rgb(41, 98, 255);\">https://app.getacceptd.com/herbalpert</u>. Neuroscience major is interdisciplinary and interdepartmental. The faculty are biologists, psychologists, biochemists, mathematicians, and engineers, all of whom share a fascination with the function of the brain. The brain is studied at many different levels, including the molecular and cellular levels, the level of systems of neurons, and the behavioral level.</p><p><br></p><p>Listed below are the lower division major preparation courses for the major as well as important details to review. THIS MAJOR IS HIGHLY SELECTIVE.</p><p><br></p><p>To be considered for this major, you must complete the following courses by the end of spring before transfer:</p><ul><li>One year of Biology for Major with Laboratory,</li><li>One year of General Chemistry with Laboratory,</li><li>One year of Calculus, and</li><li>One semester of Organic Chemistry with Lab.</li></ul><p>Completion of a second semester of Organic Chemistry or one year of Calculus Based Physics is <strong>STRONGLY RECOMMENDED</strong>. If your college does not offer a two semester or three quarter sequence in calculus-based physics, it is recommended that you complete Physics 5ABC after you transfer to UCLA.</p><p>All courses must be taken for a letter grade.</p><p><br></p><p>For more information regarding this major and UCLA's transfer selection process, visit <a href=\"http://www.eeb.ucla.edu/undegraduate\" rel=\"noopener noreferrer\" target=\"_blank\">https://www.neuroscience.ucla.edu</a> and <u style=\"color: rgb(41, 98, 255);\">https://</u><a href=\"http://www.admission.ucla.edu\" rel=\"noopener noreferrer\" target=\"_blank\">admission.ucla.edu</a>.</p><p><br></p><p>PLEASE NOTE: the community college courses listed below have been approved to satisfy the preparation requirements for this major at UCLA, but they may not be exact equivalents of the UCLA courses listed.</p>","groupId":"03bc6f45-6887-ef11-8474-000d3a37e3b6","position":1,"area":"General"},{"type":"GeneralTitle","content":"IMPORTANT MAJOR INFORMATION","groupId":"06bc6f45-6887-ef11-8474-000d3a37e3b6","position":0,"area":"General"},{"type":"RequirementTitle","content":"LOWER DIVISION MAJOR REQUIREMENTS","groupId":"352c7745-6887-ef11-8474-000d3a37e3b6","position":0,"area":"Requirements"},{"type":"GeneralTitle","content":"ADDITIONAL NOTES","groupId":"09bc6f45-6887-ef11-8474-000d3a37e3b6","position":2,"area":"General"},{"type":"GeneralText","content":"<p>UCLA's life science majors require the completion of extensive preparatory coursework prior to transfer, therefore, you must be admitted directly into a life science major; you will not be able to change from a non-life science major into a life science major after admission into UCLA.</p><p><br></p><p>Students who have placed out of UCLA's Math 31A course based on AP/IB credit may be required to complete UCLA's Math 3C, 32A or an equivalent course after transfer. The Calculus for Life Sciences courses listed below have been approved as substitutes for UCLA's Math 3ABC series through Spring 2019. However, students may be required to complete additional math courses after transfer to satisfy this requirement.</p><p><br></p><p>The community college statistics course included on this agreement has been accepted as a substitute for Statistics 13 however, it may not transfer as an exact UCLA equivalent.</p><p><br></p><p>UCLA's Chem 153A is an upper-division course that satisfies a major requirement but is NOT required for admission. After transferring, <strong><u>students must petition</u></strong> for transfer credit and should contact the academic advisor for their major for additional support and details about this process.</p>","groupId":"0cbc6f45-6887-ef11-8474-000d3a37e3b6","position":3,"area":"General"},{"type":"GeneralTitle","content":"AP/IB EXAM CREDIT","groupId":"10cf2887-4331-4657-b458-019b946c7613","position":4,"area":"General"},{"type":"GeneralText","content":"<p>The AP Exam Scores listed below may be used to satisfy the major prep:</p><ul><li>A score of <strong><u>5 on the AP Calculus AB exam</u></strong> will satisfy MATH 31A.</li><li>A score of <strong><u>4 on the AP Calculus BC exam</u></strong> will satisfy MATH 31A.</li><li>A score of <strong><u>5 on the AP Calculus BC exam</u></strong> will satisfy MATH 31A and 31B.</li></ul>","groupId":"bd394e5b-d53b-42d0-891b-019b946c7614","position":5,"area":"General"}]},{"name":"Nordic Studies/B.A.","templateAssets":[{"type":"GeneralText","content":"<p>The B.A. in Nordic Studies provides students with a robust knowledge of the cultures and histories of the Nordic countries from a global and trans-disciplinary perspective. Prelicensure Bachelor of Science (B.S.) degree program at UCLA has been designed to prepare students for a career in nursing. This is both a two and three year program. The program will focus on managing both individuals and population-based cohorts within an acute care hospital or medical center. The curriculum has been developed according to the principles of primary, secondary, and tertiary prevention; moving from a systems, population-based approach, to a cohort-based or unit- based perspective, and culminating with an intense focus on the individual-level care.</p><p>Graduates of the program will be well-prepared to deal with the demands of the present day high acuity patient populations and sophisticated technological environments. The California Board of Registered Nursing has approved this program. Graduates will be eligible to take the National Council Licensing Examination (NCLEX) to be certified as an RN after completion of the program.</p><p><br></p><p>In addition to the general UC application for admission, applicants to the nursing program must complete a supplementary application with the School of Nursing. The Nursing/Prelicensure program is not open to second baccalaureate applicants. Students with a non-nursing baccalaureate degree should apply for the Masters Entry Clinical Nurse (MSN/MECN) program.</p><p><br></p><p>For more information regarding this major and UCLA's transfer selection process, visit <u style=\"color: rgb(41, 98, 255);\">https://</u><a href=\"http://www.nursing.ucla.edu\" rel=\"noopener noreferrer\" target=\"_blank\">nursing.ucla.edu</a> and <u style=\"color: rgb(41, 98, 255);\">https://</u><a href=\"http://www.admission.ucla.edu\" rel=\"noopener noreferrer\" target=\"_blank\">admission.ucla.edu</a>.</p><p><br></p><p>Admission Requirements:</p><ul><li>Completion of specified major prerequisites with C or better grades,</li><li>A Statement of Purpose that includes an assessment of potential for nursing practice and a clear statement of goals after completion of the program,</li><li>Recommendations from two appropriate sources (teacher or counselor or professional) who has had a supervisory, educational or mentoring relationship with you,</li><li>A minimum, cumulative grade point average of 3.5 in all UC-transferable courses,</li><li>IGETC CERTIFICATION, and</li><li>Complete the University's American History and Institutions requirement.</li></ul><p><br></p><p>Consult the UCLA catalog at <u style=\"color: rgb(41, 98, 255);\">https://</u><a href=\"http://www.registar.ucla.edu\" rel=\"noopener noreferrer\" target=\"_blank\">registar.ucla.edu</a> to identify courses or examinations that satisfy this requirement.</p><p><br></p><p>PLEASE NOTE: some of the community college courses in English Composition listed on this major agreement have been approved as substitutes to satisfy the preparation requirements for this major, but they may not be exact equivalents of the UCLA courses listed. Drawing from UCLA Luskin's expansive resources in Public Policy, Social Welfare, and Urban Planning, the major combines critical thinking, social science methodology, and experiential learning, connecting the dots between theory and action. During the senior year, students complete a three-quarter experiential learning program that combines a year-long internship in a community or government organization with a seminar series in which students develop a capstone project.</p><p><br></p><p>Listed below are the lower division preparation courses for the major.</p><p><br></p><p>To be considered for this major, you must complete a <strong><u>MINIMUM OF FOUR</u></strong> major preparation courses prior to transfer:</p><ul><li>Complete One course in Microeconomics and One course in Introduction to Statistical Reasoning <strong><u>by the end of the fall prior to transfer</u></strong>; and</li><li>Complete at least Two courses from the following by the spring before transfer</li><li class=\"ql-indent-1\">Introduction to American Politics</li><li class=\"ql-indent-1\">Comparative Politics</li><li class=\"ql-indent-1\">Introduction to Political Theory</li></ul><p class=\"ql-indent-1\"><br></p><p>Students must take all major prep courses for a letter grade and receive a B grade or better in these courses to be competitive.</p><p>Additional major prep is <strong>STRONGLY RECOMMENDED</strong>.</p><p><br></p><p>To be considered for admission, applicants to the Public Affairs pre-major must have a minimum cumulative 3.2 GPA in all transferable coursework at the end of the fall. Students must attain junior level standing (at least 60 semester/90 quarter transferable units) by the end of spring prior to transfer. You must be admitted directly as a Public Affairs premajor. You will not be able to change into this major after admission to UCLA. California Community College students are strongly encouraged to complete IGETC; all other transfer students are encouraged to make progress toward completion of the Luskin School's general education Public Health major is designed for those interested in working to improve health in diverse populations. The major will introduce students to the foundations of scientific and social knowledge relevant to public health. Students learn foundational concepts and approaches regarding health issues and their solutions, explore research methods, learn to think critically about upstream and downstream approaches in the field, and use case studies and problem based learning to define issues, assess populations, implement programs, gather evidence, analyze data, and evaluate efforts. The Public Health BA and Public Health BS differ in the amount of science preparatory coursework required.</p><p><br></p><p>Listed below are the lower division preparation courses for the major.</p><p><br></p><p>To be considered for this major, you must complete a <strong><u>MINIMUM OF THREE</u></strong> major preparation courses, by the spring before transfer:</p><ul><li>One course in Cell and Molecular Biology or Life: Concepts and Issues,</li><li>One course in Chemical Structure or Chemical Principles, and</li><li>One course in Introduction to Statistical Reasoning or Statistical Methods for Life and Health Sciences.</li></ul><p>One course in Communication or an approved Writing II course is <strong>STRONGLY RECOMMENDED</strong>.</p><p>All courses must be taken for a letter grade.</p><p>Applicants must have a minimum cumulative 3.2 GPA in all transferable coursework by the end of fall.</p><p><br></p><p>For more information regarding this major and UCLA's transfer INFORMATION","groupId":"72b16f45-6887-ef11-8474-000d3a37e3b6","position":0,"area":"General"},{"type":"GeneralText","content":"<p>The School of Theater, provides a comprehensive introduction to the history, theory, and practice of these art forms within the context of a liberal arts education. Undergraduates in Theater study the history of world and American theater, contemporary theater issues, acting and performance, play-writing and analysis, design, directing, theater production, and complete a sequence of advanced courses in their chosen emphases along with a capstone course.</p><p><br></p><p>Applicants interested in the Theater major must choose one of the following emphasis on the UC Application: Acting, Design/ Production, Musical Theater, or Integrated Studies. Students interested in Directing or Play-writing, Teaching Artistry and Theater/Performance should apply through Integrated Studies. Those interested in Stage Management should select Design/Production.</p><p><br></p><p>In addition to the general UC Application, a <a href=\"https://admission.ucla.edu/apply/supplemental-applications\" rel=\"noopener noreferrer\" target=\"_blank\">supplemental application</a> is required. This includes materials such as a headshot, writing samples, transcripts, resumes, etc. Applicants will be contacted ONLY if more information is needed and an interview/ audition will be required. Note: Transfer students cannot change to the Theater major after admission to UCLA.</p><p><br></p><p>Additional information may be found at the <a href=\"https://www.tft.ucla.edu/programs/theater-ba/\" rel=\"noopener noreferrer\" target=\"_blank\">Theater B.A. page</a>.</p><p><br></p><p>Applicants to the school must have a minimum 3.2 GPA at the time of application and by the time of entrance must have attained junior standing (60 semester/90 quarter units) and have completed their general education coursework— either the school’s GE requirements, the IGETC at a California community college, or the GE requirements while a student at another UC campus. Completion of the School of Theater, Film and Television's foreign language requirement before arriving at UCLA is strongly encouraged but not required. In addition to the UC application, applicants are required to submit a supplemental application. Transfer students cannot change to the Theater major after they transfer to UCLA.</p><p><br></p><p>Recommended preparation for the major: Acting, Design, Play Analysis, and Theater History.</p><p><br></p><p>For more information regarding this major and UCLA's transfer selection process, visit <u style=\"color: rgb(41, 98, 255);\">https://</u><a href=\"http://www.tft.ucla.edu/theaterba\" rel=\"noopener noreferrer\" target=\"_blank\">tft.ucla.edu/theaterba</a> and <u style=\"color: rgb(41, 98, 255);\">https://</u><a href=\"http://www.admission.ucla.edu\" rel=\"noopener noreferrer\" target=\"_blank\">admission.ucla.edu</a>.</p>","groupId":"80b16f45-6887-ef11-8474-000d3a37e3b6","position":1,"area":"General"}]},{"name":"World Arts and Cultures/B.A.","templateAssets":[{"type":"GeneralTitle","content":"IMPORTANT MAJOR INFORMATION","groupId":"c0b06f45-6887-ef11-8474-000d3a37e3b6","position":0,"area":"General"},{"type":"GeneralText","content":"<p>The B.A. in World Arts and Cultures (WAC) enables students to critically examine and constructively engage the social and cultural contexts that shape artists and their creativity. Our interdisciplinary curriculum accentuates those local histories and global influences that inform ethnographic, curatorial, creative and scholarly praxis, as well as activist politics and questions of social justice.</p><p><br></p><p>The WAC major encourages students to understand the making and reception of arts and social movements through a critical lens that is rooted in a range of cultural and post-colonial theories. As such, education in this major is built on the dialogue between theory and practice, between creative work and critical analysis. Our faculty have specialties ranging from documentary film making and theory, health and healing, community engagement, ethnography, critical curatorial studies, research methodologies, critical race studies, art direction, digital culture and surveillance studies, Indigenous studies, prison abolition, spoken word, feminist theory and more. </p><p><br></p><p>The most important admission criteria are the supplemental application which involves additional essays, strong academic performance, and evidence of community engagement relative to interest in the major.</p><p><br></p><p>Preparation for the major:</p><ul><li>All preparatory coursework for the major should be completed at UCLA. Your individual interests related to the WAC the major can be shown through your IGETC coursework selection. Substitutions for lower-division requirements will be determined by the department in the summer following admission. Syllabi or other descriptive course documentation may be required for consideration.</li></ul><p><br></p><p>Supplemental Requirements:</p><p>In addition to the general UC Application, applicants must submit a supplement which consists of major-specific essays. Additional fees may apply. We will also be looking for strong academic preparation and evidence of involvement in the arts and community that demonstrates interest in varied cultures. </p><p><br></p><p>All students must have a cumulative 3.0 GPA at the time of the application.</p><p><strong>Students must complete the requisite two English courses and one Math course by the end of Spring prior to transfer.</strong> Students are encouraged to take their required English and Math courses as early as possible with at least one English course completed by the end of Fall.</p><p>Completion of IGETC is not required but strongly recommended.</p><p><br></p><p>More information may be found at <a href=\"https://arts.ucla.edu/apply\" rel=\"noopener noreferrer\" target=\"_blank\" style=\"color: rgb(41, 98, 255);\"><u>https://arts.ucla.edu/apply</u></a>. World Arts and Cultures considers sophomore transfers.</p><p><br></p><p>For more information about sophomore transfer admission criteria, please visit <a href=\"https://arts.ucla.edu/apply\" rel=\"noopener noreferrer\" target=\"_blank\" style=\"color: rgb(41, 98, 255);\"><u>https://arts.ucla.edu/apply</u></a>.</p>","groupId":"c4b06f45-6887-ef11-8474-000d3a37e3b6","position":1,"area":"General"}]}]
